mode: Built-in image_gen tool for poster and box artwork; existing Browser/dist/favicon.svg exported directly for tile icons.
requirement: Every frontal view must show the central frontage, with both blue heraldic dragons and the coat of arms above the entrance.

prompts.initialPoster:
Use case: compositing / ads-marketing.
Transform the two reference screenshots into one finished Microsoft Store portrait cover for the game "Escape from 1829".
Image 1 is the actual game landing screen: use it for the established forest-green, sage and warm ivory brand palette, elegant large serif title, and the low-poly historic hospital architecture. Image 2 is the actual main entrance: preserve its red brick, white sash windows, pale basement, red central door, paired pale columns, dark railing and broad stepped entrance. These are reference images, not elements to show as screenshots.
Create an atmospheric but restrained, beautifully composed game cover in a 2:3 portrait aspect ratio, ideally 1440 x 2160 pixels. It must remain recognisable as this stylised 3D game, with architectural forms closely grounded in the references rather than an invented gothic castle. Show the central hospital frontage and entrance, with a little of its long wings. A deep forest-green evening atmosphere and subtle pale mist on the approach, warm ivory highlights, red brick and subdued sage shadows. No characters, no monsters, no extra towers.
Place the exact title, and no other text, in the upper half: "ESCAPE" on the first line, a smaller "FROM" on the second, and large "1829" on the third. Refined high-contrast Roman serif lettering resembling Georgia, warm ivory, perfectly spelled, carefully spaced, easily readable at thumbnail size. Keep all title text inside the upper 60% and leave generous safe margins. The main building sits across the centre to lower middle; the bottom third contains atmospheric approach/ground without important text, allowing Store overlays.
Finished edge-to-edge opaque artwork: no frame, no UI, no buttons, no map, no watermarks, no ratings, no Microsoft/Xbox branding, no promotional claims. One portrait cover only, not a collage or a set of variants.
prompts.correctedPoster:
Use case: precise-object-edit / ads-marketing.
Edit reference image 1, the portrait Escape from 1829 cover, to correct the hospital building using reference images 2 and 3, which are actual photographs of its entrance. Keep the refined ivory serif title reading exactly "ESCAPE" / "FROM" / "1829", the deep green evening palette, atmospheric approach, elegant composition and opaque full-bleed portrait format. Export a single 2:3 poster, ideally exactly 1440x2160 pixels.
CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL CORRECTION: the defining feature MUST be clearly visible: the LARGE white-edged triangular pediment crowning the central frontage, filled across its width with TWO vivid BLUE heraldic dragons and curling blue tails flanking the gold-and-blue CENTRAL COAT OF ARMS, accurately following the photographs. This is an architectural painted relief within the triangular pediment, not flying dragons or animals in the sky. Do not reduce it to a small generic triangle, erase it, obscure it in mist or leaves, or substitute plain brick.
Correct the central frontage to the real THREE-storey red-brick central block above the pale basement: three white sash windows on the upper row below the dragon pediment, three sash windows on the next row, and the red entrance door with flanking sash windows at the lower main level. White horizontal stringcourses, pale window lintels, and the columned portico with paired white columns, raised red doorway, dark railing and steps must match the photos. Keep the roof pediment, all blue dragon relief, entrance and both outer sides of the central frontage wholly inside frame. Side wings can extend outside frame. Avoid invented facades, extra towers and roof shapes.
Use a polished atmospheric stylised game-cover render grounded in those exact architectural features. The blue heraldic dragons should remain saturated and readable despite the dusk lighting. Frame the building large enough to recognise them at thumbnail size. Keep title within upper 40%, with generous margins; keep important architecture within the upper-to-middle two-thirds where possible. Bottom is quiet foreground for Store overlays. No other text, UI, borders, logos, watermarks, people, monsters or rating badges.
